_note: Where to find a hero photograph for a journey the Virtuoso API has never heard of.
Every card on the five journey atlases takes its picture from the supplier's own
`defaultImageUrl`, except the 27 bespoke jet journeys — 18 Safrans du Monde and 9
National Geographic — which we built ourselves and which therefore arrive with no
photograph at all. A card with no picture beside cards that have one does not read as
'no photo available', it reads as broken.
This ledger names the page each journey's photograph should come from.
scripts/harvest-journey-photos.mjs reads it, pulls the hero out of each page, and
writes the answers to journey-photos.json, which the merge then applies. The two files
are separate on purpose: this one is edited by a person and the other is generated, so
a supplier redesigning their site costs a re-run rather than a re-research.
`collector` says how to read the page:
og       the page's og:image / twitter:image meta tag — the supplier's own hero.
safrans  the journey table inside public/safrans-du-monde.html, matched on the
`#sdm-…` anchor these trips already link to. Local, so it needs no network
and cannot drift from the promo page a guest sees for the same journey.
A journey with no entry here keeps no photograph, and that is a deliberate outcome
rather than a gap to paper over: better one plate-coloured card than a stock picture
of somewhere the journey does not go.

sources.note: National Geographic has published no public trip page for this 2027 departure yet — only a terms page and a press release, neither carrying an og:image. Paste the trip page here when it goes live.
